subsystems.name: Bidirectional charger
subsystems.role: converts DC battery energy into grid-compatible AC and back, and isolates the vehicle from the grid.

subsystems.name: Vehicle battery and management system
subsystems.role: stores energy and enforces limits on discharge to protect battery life and warranty.

subsystems.name: Communication and control link
subsystems.role: carries commands and data between vehicle, charger, aggregator and grid operator.

subsystems.name: Aggregation and dispatch platform
subsystems.role: groups thousands of vehicles into a controllable virtual battery and trades its capacity.

subsystems.name: Grid interface and protection
subsystems.role: connects the aggregated resource safely to the distribution network and meets grid codes.

buildSteps.title: Make the charger bidirectional
buildSteps.detail: Design power electronics that can both rectify grid AC to DC for charging and invert DC to AC for export, with efficiency above 95% and galvanic isolation.

buildSteps.title: Enable the vehicle
buildSteps.detail: Update battery management firmware to allow controlled discharge, and add hardware in models not originally built for it.

buildSteps.title: Standardise the connection
buildSteps.detail: Adopt connectors and protocols — CCS with ISO 15118, or CHAdeMO — so any compatible car and charger can negotiate power flow.

buildSteps.title: Install charging points
buildSteps.detail: Deploy bidirectional wallboxes at homes, depots and workplaces, wired for higher export currents than one-way chargers.

buildSteps.title: Build the aggregation software
buildSteps.detail: Write algorithms that predict when cars will be plugged in and how much energy they can safely spare, then bid that capacity into grid markets.

buildSteps.title: Qualify with the grid
buildSteps.detail: Meet the local distribution and transmission operator's requirements for protection, metering and response time.

buildSteps.title: Run pilots and scale
buildSteps.detail: Start with fleet vehicles that have predictable schedules, then extend to homes and public chargers as confidence grows.

buildSteps.title: Operate and settle
buildSteps.detail: Continuously monitor availability, dispatch, and pay owners for energy and services delivered.

prerequisites.why: only some EV models today can export power; many lack the hardware or firmware.
ISO 15118 and CHAdeMO already define vehicle-to-grid messaging, and OCPP links chargers to backends.

prerequisites.tech: Grid codes and market rules for aggregated resources
prerequisites.why: some regions allow small resources to provide frequency response, but rules vary and often require minimum capacities.
accurate measurement is needed to bill and settle, and smart meters are widely deployed.
thousands of internet-connected chargers widen the attack surface, and defences are still maturing.

pathway.milestone: Fleet and pilot projects such as electric buses and delivery vans demonstrate V2G for frequency regulation and peak shaving.
pathway.unlocks: proven hardware and market rules for larger rollouts.

pathway.milestone: Home V2G offered with specific car and charger combinations, enabling households to earn from parked cars.
Aggregators combine thousands of vehicles into virtual power plants that bid into wholesale and ancillary markets.
pathway.unlocks: grid flexibility at scale, deferring network upgrades.

pathway.milestone: V2G as a standard feature of EVs and chargers, integrated with renewable forecasting and dynamic pricing.
pathway.unlocks: a resilient, low-carbon grid where transport and power sectors share storage.
